question: When an Adapter contract calls PPA Core, does Core observe the Adapter or the original initiating EOA?
answer: CORE OBSERVES THE ADAPTER. The original EOA identity is consumed at the adapter hop.

scope.nature: throwaway probes; no PPA edits, no capability change, no deployment
scope.environment: GLSim localnet on :4000 via gltest, genlayer-py 0.18 / genlayer-test 0.29, pinned runner py-genlayer:1jb45aa8ynh2a9c9xn3b7qqh8sm5q93hwfp7jqmwsfhh8jpz09h6

observations.note: the JSON declared_source flowed through untouched; the true caller remained the Adapter

enforcementProof.case: C registered adapter widens amount to 99999
enforcementProof.note: Core saw the widened value and rejected it independently; the Adapter cannot widen

enforcementProof.case: D adapter observed vs core observed
enforcementProof.note: identity is consumed at the hop

selectedModel: Core sees the Adapter -> use a Core trusted-adapter registry plus an Adapter trusted-adjudicator registry.
designConsequences: Core authenticates the Adapter via gl.message.sender_address, never via a JSON field.
Adapter authenticates the adjudicator via the sender it observes when the adjudicator calls it.
Core CANNOT know which human initiated the request. It authenticates the Adapter, which is the correct and intended trust boundary.
Core must independently recheck account policy, amount, recipient, capital and replay. The spike proves an Adapter cannot widen amount beyond a Core-side cap.
A JSON source_contract field is worthless as provenance; the spoof case demonstrates it.
emit() is ASYNCHRONOUS: Core runs in a later transaction. The boundary is not atomic.

Core must NOT raise to signal refusal on an emitted call. A raise reverts the emitted transaction and leaves NO observable artifact; the Adapter and any observer then cannot learn why. Proven during this spike: a rejecting raise produced an absent log, and the identical logic changed to return a verdict produced a readable verdict. Refusal must be a returned status.
Reads after an emit must poll; the emitted transaction is not immediately visible.
Appeal hazard: if the emitting transaction is appealed after emit(), the emitted call still executes (per the write-contract skill). Core-side revalidation is the mitigation.
notClaimed: This spike used GLSim localnet, not Bradbury. Semantics are expected to match but must be re-proven live before the split is trusted.
The probe proves the caller-identity model and that Core can bound an Adapter. It does NOT prove that the real PPA Core and Adapter enforce correctly; that is Work Contract 2's job.
Nothing here was deployed. No PPA source was modified.
verdictForDesign: ADAPTER_ORIGIN_MODEL_SUPPORTED. The two-registry design is viable and does not require any signed-receipt or proof-carrying mechanism, because Core can authenticate the Adapter from the sender address alone.
